explanation: Relocation is a crucial step in the linking process where the final addresses of functions and variables are determined and patched into the executable.  Because code often needs to reference data and functions whose addresses aren't known until link time (or even load time), relocation is essential for creating executable files that can run in different memory locations. Without it, each program would have to be loaded at the same memory address every time.
